title: Rivetus and Sohn: certain fiducia that remission and life are granted to me in particular
source_text: LVI. Similiter Rivetus, in fidei definitione quam supra attulimus, tribuit illi Certam fiduciam per quam unusquisque fidelis, in Deo acquiescens firmiter statuit, non solum in genere promissam esse credentibus remissionem peccatorum, sed sibi in particulari concessam, aeternamque justitiam, & ex ea vitam, ex Dei misericordia, propter unius Jesu Christi meritum donatam esse. Eodem modo Sohnus, saeculo superiori Theologiae Professor in Academia Heydelbergensi, fiduciam, quam habet pro parte potissima fidei justificantis, dicit esse Qua non tantum promissioni gratiae generaliter assentimur, sed etiam nobis quisque promissionem istam applicamus, certo statuentes eam ad nos quoque pertinere; id est, non tantum alios, sed nos quoque Deum habere propitium, juxta promissionem gratiae; ideoque in Christo, & per Christum in Deo prorsus acquiescimus & laetamur. Oper. Sohnii, t. 2. p. 789.
pass_a_gloss: Similarly Rivetus, in the definition of faith which we brought above, attributes to it a Sure trust by which each of the faithful, resting in God, firmly lays down that remission of sins is promised to believers not only in general, but granted to himself in particular, and that eternal justice, and life from it, have been given from God's mercy for the merit of the one Jesus Christ. In the same way Sohn, formerly Professor of Theology in the Heidelberg Academy, says that trust, which he holds for the chief part of justifying faith, is that by which we not only assent generally to the promise of grace, but also each of us applies that promise to ourselves, certainly laying down that it pertains to us also; that is, that not only others, but we also have God propitious, according to the promise of grace; and therefore in Christ, and through Christ in God, we altogether rest and rejoice. Works of Sohn, volume 2, page 789.
pass_b_english: Rivetus: sure fiducia — remission not only in general but mine; eternal justice and life for Christ’s merit.
Sohn (Heidelberg): chief part of justifying faith = apply the grace-promise to myself.
Not only others — I too have God propitious; rest and rejoice in God through Christ.
